question: What is the main job of emergency contraception?

options.A: To terminate an established pregnancy safely
options.B: To serve as a regular daily family planning method
options.C: To prevent pregnancy after unprotected intercourse
options.D: To protect against sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Think of emergency contraception as your backup plan after a contraceptive slip-up or unprotected sex. It is not meant for daily family planning and doesn't work if a pregnancy has already started. You've got this!

question: Why do nurses need to explain that emergency contraceptives are not abortifacients?

options.A: To show that they can also cure sexually transmitted infections
options.B: To prove that the drugs are 100 percent effective every time
options.C: To encourage patients to use them instead of regular condoms
options.D: To clear up cultural and moral misconceptions about how the drugs work

explanation: A lot of people mix up emergency pills with abortion pills. As a nurse, clarifying how it actually works helps calm unnecessary fears and clears up social myths. Brilliant work!

question: What is the single most important factor for emergency contraception to work successfully?

options.A: The time of day the client ate their last meal
options.B: The age and weight of the client receiving the pill
options.C: The brand name of the emergency contraceptive drug
options.D: The timing of administration after unprotected sex

explanation: Time is everything with emergency contraception! The sooner you take it after unprotected sex, the better it works. Don't leave it too late!

question: A client comes to the clinic saying her partner's condom tore three hours ago. What advice should you give?

options.A: Avoid emergency contraception because it only works after 72 hours
options.B: Wait exactly 48 hours before taking any action to let natural cycles adjust
options.C: Come back next week for a pregnancy test before doing anything
options.D: Take the emergency contraceptive as soon as possible for the highest effectiveness

explanation: When accidents happen like a torn condom, acting fast is key. Taking the pill right away gives the client the highest chance of preventing a pregnancy.

question: How do standard hormonal emergency contraceptive pills stop a pregnancy from happening?

options.A: By destroying a fertilized egg that is already implanted
options.B: By permanently stopping the normal production of estrogen
options.C: By thickening the bladder lining to trap excess hormones
options.D: By delaying or preventing the release of an egg from the ovary

explanation: Hormonal emergency pills simply hit the pause button on ovulation. If no egg is released, the sperm has nothing to fertilize. Simple and clever!

question: Why won't hormonal emergency pills work if a woman has already ovulated?

options.A: Because the hormone dose is too low to stay in the stomach
options.B: Because the egg has already been released and is available for fertilization
options.C: Because ovulation automatically neutralizes all chemical drugs
options.D: Because the uterine lining instantly sheds upon ovulation

explanation: Remember, these pills work by delaying ovulation. If the egg has already been released, the pill is too late to stop it from meeting a sperm. Makes total sense, right?

question: Within what window of time should standard levonorgestrel emergency pills be taken for the best result?

options.B: At any time during the entire monthly cycle
options.C: Exactly 24 hours after the next menstrual period

explanation: Levonorgestrel (like the popular Postinor-2) works best when taken within 72 hours (3 days) after unprotected sex. Keep this rule of thumb handy!

question: How does ulipristal acetate compare to levonorgestrel in terms of its time window?

options.A: Ulipristal must be taken within the first 12 hours only
options.B: Ulipristal is only used for regular daily birth control
options.C: Ulipristal can remain effective for up to 120 hours after intercourse
options.D: Ulipristal requires surgical insertion by a trained doctor

explanation: Ulipristal gives a bit more breathing room, staying effective for up to 120 hours (5 days) after unprotected sex. You're mastering pharmacology step by step!

question: What makes the copper IUD special compared to emergency contraceptive pills?

options.A: It is only effective if taken within the first two hours
options.B: It must be swallowed as a tablet with a full glass of water
options.C: It provides ongoing long-term birth control after emergency use
options.D: It permanently stops a woman from ever having children

explanation: The copper IUD is a double-whammy: it works as emergency contraception right now, and it can stay in place to prevent pregnancy for years. Super convenient!

question: How soon after unprotected sex must a copper IUD be inserted to act as emergency contraception?

options.A: Up to 30 days after the event

explanation: A copper IUD can be put in place up to 5 days (120 hours) after unprotected sex and still successfully prevent pregnancy. You're doing great!

question: Why is asking about the last menstrual period crucial during an emergency contraception assessment?

options.A: To check if the patient is already pregnant from a previous cycle
options.B: To calculate the exact date of birth for the current month
options.C: To determine how much weight the patient has recently gained
options.D: To verify if the patient has regular sleeping habits

explanation: Always check the last menstrual period first! Emergency contraception won't help if the client is already pregnant from an earlier cycle. Great clinical thinking!

question: What attitude should you always show when counseling a client who needs emergency contraception?
explanation: As nurses, our job is to provide a safe, private, and judgment-free space so clients feel comfortable seeking help without fear of stigma. Excellent nursing values!

question: What common side effects should you warn a client about after taking hormonal emergency contraception?

options.A: Temporary nausea, headache, or irregular spotting
options.B: Sudden swelling of the lower limbs
options.C: Complete cessation of all future menstrual cycles
options.D: Permanent loss of vision in both eyes

explanation: A sudden rush of hormones can make clients feel a bit nauseous, tired, or give them a mild headache. Reassure them that this is totally normal and temporary!

question: A client vomits twenty minutes after taking her emergency contraceptive pill. What should you do?

options.A: Ignore the vomiting because it has no effect on the medication
options.B: Consult the provider to see if a repeat dose is needed
options.C: Give her a high dose of intravenous antibiotics immediately
options.D: Tell her the pill failed and she must schedule surgery

explanation: If she vomits shortly after taking the pill (within two hours), her body might not have absorbed the medicine. Always check with the clinician if she needs another dose!

question: Which of these statements about emergency contraception pills is FALSE?

options.A: They are most effective when taken soon after intercourse
options.B: They work by delaying the release of an egg from the ovary
options.C: They cause permanent and irreversible infertility in women
options.D: They do not protect against sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Emergency pills do NOT make a woman barren! Their hormonal effect is short-term and has zero effect on future fertility. Busting myths like a pro!

question: A young student in Nigeria worries that taking Postinor-2 will make her barren. How should you respond?

options.A: Prescribe a strong surgical procedure to clear her reproductive system
options.B: Scold her for engaging in premarital sex and refuse to give her the medication
options.C: Gently educate her with facts, explaining that the drug does not cause permanent infertility
options.D: Agree with her fears and advise her never to use any form of family planning

explanation: Market myths can be scary! Gently talking clients through the facts builds trust and ensures they get safe, accurate reproductive healthcare. You're going to be an amazing nurse!
